sub: The costume is the small risk — these are the ones that fill clinics

cards.title: Toxic — Call, Don't Wait
rows: Keep the wrapper for the dose

cards.title: The Front Door
rows: This is the night pets get out
Pet in a closed back room
TV on, water, something to chew
On your phone, just in case

cards.title: Decorations To Move
list: Real candles in pumpkins — tails knock them over
Glow sticks and glow necklaces — bitter, and the casing obstructs
Small props a pet can swallow
Dry ice — burns and displaces air at floor level

cards.title: Before The First Knock
checks: Candy bowl out of reach, not on a low table
Pet in the back room with the TV on
Doors and gates checked, windows shut
Collar on, tag readable, chip details current
Vet and out-of-hours numbers in your phone
A long walk or hard play session this afternoon

cards.title: Call A Vet Tonight
list: ANY xylitol or birch sugar — before symptoms
Repeated vomiting, tremors, collapse or seizures
Retching with nothing coming up, hard belly — bloat
Any swallowed wrapper, stick or costume part

rules_post: People Get Wrong On The Night
rules: Leaving the candy bowl at pet height.
It is the single most dangerous object in the house that evening, and it sits where a dog can reach it all night.
Assuming xylitol is less serious than chocolate.
It is more urgent. A few pieces of sugar-free gum can crash a dog's blood sugar and damage the liver.
Crowds, masks at face height, children running and dropped candy on every sidewalk. This is the night dogs bolt.
Thinking a sociable dog will be fine with masks.
Dogs read faces using eyes and mouth together. A mask removes the mouth and leaves something human-shaped and wrong.
Looking up the emergency number at 10pm.
With a distressed animal in your arms is the worst possible time. Write it down this afternoon.
